text:
Nina (AE): Heads-up — BigCorp renewal in 6 weeks. They just escalated: asking for a formal SLA (99.99% uptime + p95 < 200ms) and a dedicated capacity option. They said it's a must-have for renewal.
Alex (PM): Thanks. Can we get a quick read on effort and risk? We need numbers to push back / negotiate. Also thinking RICE-style prioritization vs roadmap.
Ryan (Eng): Engineering quick take: dedicated capacity + SLA runbook = infra + infra-ops + monitoring work. Rough estimate: ~3 dev-weeks to wire capacity reservations + autoscale tweaks, + 1 week for SLA monitoring/playbook and runbook. KMS + audit might be extra if they want on-prem keys. Confidence: medium-low.
Jess (CS): Customer stats: ~500k API requests/day, high concurrency during batch runs. Revenue tied to them ~ $1.2M ARR. They're already seeing occasional slowdowns during bursts — that's why they're pushing. Renewal probability drops fast if we don't show a plan.
Nina (AE): Sales note: they're not asking for no-questions SLA forever — they're open to a timeboxed commitment if we can offer a migration path to Dedicated. They asked for exact wording by EOD Monday.
Alex (PM): Ok. Two axes: (A) Accept full SLA now (fast but high engineering cost + roadmap disruption) (B) Offer conditional SLA tied to Dedicated onboarding + limited canary (lower cost, lower immediate risk). Need a short RICE-ish run to compare.
Ryan (Eng): Also operational note: fallback policy required — if we miss targets, what do we do? Credits? Rate-limits? Default fallback has to be in-contract. Building automatic fallback takes more time; manual ops is quicker.
Alex (PM): Quick RICE calc (very rough) — posting as a snippet:
```
reach = 1  # single big logo but big ARR
impact = 8  # high impact on revenue/renewal
confidence = 0.6
effort = 20  # person-days across infra + SRE + compliance
RICE = (reach * impact * confidence) / effort
RICE ≈ (1 * 8 * 0.6) / 20 = 0.24
```
Interpretation: low numeric RICE because effort is high, but business criticality skews decision toward making an exception.
Jess (CS): Agreed — RICE doesn't capture churn risk well for single big logos. Recommend product-level exception path: short-term SLA + pilot Dedicated + clear migration timeline.
Nina (AE): Sales ask: if we offer 3-month temporary SLA (99.9%) + dedicated pilot with a 6 month commit, they will sign. They want SLAs in contract wording though.
Ryan (Eng): Technical tradeoff: we can stand up a limited dedicated pool + enhanced monitoring for the pilot in ~2-3 weeks if we repurpose capacity and do manual ops. Fully automated autoscale + SLO enforcement will take longer.
Alex (PM): Proposal: Offer two-track response to customer:
- Option A (fast): 3-month temporary SLA at 99.9% + dedicated pilot (manual ops, limited scale). Requires minimal infra changes, target delivery 2-3 weeks.
- Option B (long): Full 99.99% SLA tied to Dedicated with platform changes (autoscale, runbook, compliance). Delivery 8+ weeks, requires roadmap reprioritization.
We should present both and make the long-term SLA contingent on commit.
Jess (CS): I'll draft the customer-facing note for Nina. Make sure we add escalation playbook and 'service credits' language for Option A.
Nina (AE): Please cc legal. Sales will push for 99.99 but they'll accept Option A if it's temporary and we show timeline for Option B.
Ryan (Eng): Action items for eng: estimate exact capacity delta for pilot, checklist for manual run, and SLO monitoring dashboard. I'll do that by Wed.
Alex (PM): I'll score this against current roadmap items and propose swap candidates. If product signs off, we ship Option A as a negotiated commitment and schedule Option B into the next release cycle.
oncall-bot: Reminder — deploy freeze tomorrow 00:00-04:00 UTC. Keep that window in mind for any pilot provisioning. :warning:
Alex (PM): Good call — account for the freeze in timelines. Jess/Nina, I'll share a one-pager to land with Legal and Sales by EOD today.
Jess (CS): Thanks — ping me when it's ready, I'll review for tone and churn-risk language.
Nina (AE): Thx team. I'll set a customer call after we have the two options drafted. :thumbsup:
